rounds.title: Logistics Analytics Interview
rounds.description: Advanced network-operations interview on SLA, throughput, warehouse capacity, cost and executive decision support using synthetic data.

questions.context: The interviewer asks which routes have the highest late-shipment workload.
questions.prompt: Using logistics_shipments, return route_code and COUNT(*) AS late_shipments for rows where actual_hours > promised_hours, grouped by route_code.
questions.explanation: A correct answer isolates late shipments before grouping. This measures observed workload, not the root cause of delay.

questions.context: Saturday forecast demand exceeds planned throughput by 70 shipments.
questions.prompt: What is the strongest first recommendation?
options: Treat the gap as a planning signal, validate forecast error and test staffing, routing or capacity scenarios before rollout
Assume exactly 70 shipments will fail every Saturday
Remove the Saturday forecast from the report
questions.expectedAnswer: Treat the gap as a planning signal, validate forecast error and test staffing, routing or capacity scenarios before rollout
questions.explanation: Forecast gaps support scenario planning under uncertainty; they are not guaranteed failure counts.

questions.context: A route has weak SLA and high normalized cost. Leadership asks whether it should be redesigned.
questions.prompt: Describe how you would structure the analysis before recommending a network change.
questions.explanation: A strong network case separates service, cost, shipment mix and capacity before recommending a controlled routing or operating change.
